issues.description: Method 'check_status': the problem statement (problem_statement.md) requires that check_status return a Boolean value (0 or 1) in EAX, but the solution implementation in solution/helloWorld.asm stores the address of the 'hello' data label into EAX (mov eax, hello). This means the solution returns a pointer instead of the specified boolean, which will conflict with any grading or runtime checks that expect 0/1 in EAX and will confuse students about the expected return convention.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the implementation of check_status so that it places exactly 0 or 1 in EAX before returning. For example, to return false: xor eax, eax; ret. To return true: xor eax, eax; mov al, 1; ret. Ensure the function's behavior matches the problem statement's contract (EAX == 0 or 1).

issues.description: Register name inconsistency: the template assembly file (helloWorld.asm in the template) uses the invalid identifier 'ecc' in the instruction 'add eax, ecc', while the problem statement and the solution use the correct x86 register name 'ecx'. The typo in the template will cause assembly/compilation errors and prevents students from building the project until corrected.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the register name in the template file from 'ecc' to 'ecx' (change the instruction to 'add eax, ecx') so that the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use 'ecx' and the project compiles successfully.
